mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for two consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A double-digit year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) combined with a concurrent drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals a sharp contraction in aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY < -10% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to produce a statistically significant negative median return.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPI above 6% combined with a simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate signals an aggressive inflation-fighting cycle, which increases uncertainty and discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > previous month +6% AND FEDFUNDS > previous month +0.25%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism's predictive power is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by >0.3pp for 3 consecutive months (i.e., rising unemployment)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based demand expansion, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA AND HOUST > 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for six consecutive months signals a broad-based supply expansion, which increases corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during periods when INDPRO rises for six consecutive months at 5% significance.
